purpose: External check on the N2 active-space ladder above the exact wall. The 28-orbital rung is full CI in this basis (1.4e12 determinants) and has no internal reference; these are published near-exact values for the same Hamiltonian.
provenance_note: Numerical values transcribed from the published tables of the cited papers. No data repository is involved and no licence is claimed over them; they are cited facts, re-derivable by anyone running the same calculation.
unit_trap: The two sources use DIFFERENT geometry units. Chan/Kallay/Gauss and the CDFCI curve built on it quote bond lengths in BOHR (equilibrium 2.118 a0); the SHCI dimer table quotes ANGSTROM (1.0977 A). 2.118 a0 = 1.12079733272856 A with pyscf's BOHR = 0.52917721092, so these are two different geometries 0.023 A apart, not one geometry in two units.
basis_note: cc-pVDZ with spherical (pure) d functions, giving 28 spatial orbitals for N2. Cartesian d would give 30 and a different energy. Confirmed by reproducing the published RHF energy at 2.118 a0 to 2.1e-8 Ha, which is that value's own rounding.

citations.chan2004: G. K.-L. Chan, M. Kallay, J. Gauss, 'State-of-the-art density matrix renormalization group and coupled cluster theory studies of the nitrogen binding curve', J. Chem. Phys. 121, 6110-6116 (2004). Source of the 2.118 a0 equilibrium geometry and of the DMRG value.
citations.cdfci2019: Z. Wang, Y. Li, J. Lu, 'Coordinate descent full configuration interaction', J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2019), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00138, arXiv:1902.04592. Source of the CDFCI, CCSD, CCSDTQ, MRCISD and MRCCSD values and of the RHF energy in its Table 1.
citations.shci2017: S. Sharma, A. A. Holmes, G. Jeanmairet, A. Alavi, C. J. Umrigar, 'Semistochastic Heat-bath Configuration Interaction method: selected configuration interaction with semistochastic perturbation theory', J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2017), doi:10.1021/acs.jctc.6b01028, arXiv:1610.06660. Source of the frozen-core value.

all_electron.determinant_note: The CDFCI paper quotes 1.75e11 for the same space; that is this count divided by the D2h order of 8. Our ladder runs in C1 and quotes the undivided count.
all_electron.uncertainty_note: CDFCI and the independent DMRG of Chan et al. differ by 1.6e-5 Ha; CCSDTQ sits 2.3e-4 above. The spread between the two near-exact methods is taken as the uncertainty. CDFCI's own convergence table reaches 1e-5 of this value.
all_electron.source: cdfci2019 Table 1 and Table 5; DMRG row attributed there to chan2004

frozen_core.uncertainty_note: Quoted as -109.2769(1): a statistical error of 1 in the last printed digit, from the semistochastic perturbative correction. The value is therefore not variational and resolves only at 1e-4.
frozen_core.source: shci2017 Table I, row 'N2 DZ', epsilon_1 = 5e-4
frozen_core.convention_note: This source publishes no HF energy for N2, so its basis convention cannot be checked the way the all-electron one was. The agreement itself certifies it: a spherical/Cartesian mismatch would show up as a discrepancy of order 1e-2 Ha, and the observed difference is 1.9e-5. Note also that our DMRG energy sits ABOVE this value, as a variational upper bound must against a near-exact number carrying a perturbative correction.

all_electron_curve.description: The published all-electron binding curve, which lets our EXISTING geometries be checked without running anything at a new bond length. Two of the three fall inside it; 2.4 Angstrom = 4.535 a0 does not, and extrapolating to it is refused.
all_electron_curve.uncertainty_note: The curve and the converged headline value coincide at 2.118 a0, so the curve is taken to carry the same uncertainty as that value: the CDFCI/DMRG spread of 1.6e-5, rounded to 2e-5.
all_electron_curve.interpolation_note: Between grid points the curve must be interpolated, and that adds its own error. It is measured, not assumed: leave-one-out cubic-spline prediction of each interior published point is accurate to 6.2e-5 Ha at worst over the whole curve and about 1.0e-5 near both geometries this project checks. See n2_curve_energy(). The estimate is conservative by construction: leaving a point out doubles the local grid spacing, so it is measured across a gap twice as wide as any real query sits inside.
